audit_items.audit_summary: The commitment_indices bounds validation is delegated to external c-kzg-4844 library. Erigon's VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs (cl/das/p2p_utils.go:50-79) passes cellIndices directly to ckzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. The index bounds validation occurs within the external library, not in Erigon code. P2P gossip validation layer calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar which checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns but this is column index validation, not commitment_indices within batch.

Remote crash potential via crafted commitment_indices depends on c-kzg-4844 library behavior. Erigon wraps the call at cl/das/p2p_utils.go:73 with error handling (lines 74-77) that converts library errors to false return. Go's memory safety prevents direct crash from out-of-bounds, but library behavior determines actual crash vectors.

Memory safety of verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl is determined by c-kzg-4844 implementation (C library with Go bindings). Erigon is written in Go which provides memory safety, but c-kzg-4844 uses CGO to call into C code. The actual memory safety depends on the external library's C implementation, not Erigon's Go wrapper.

PARTIALLY VERIFIED: Erigon validates that KzgCommitments.Len() == KzgProofs.Len() at cl/das/p2p_utils.go:41-43. However, the full four-array length validation (commitment_bytes, cell_indices, cells, proofs_bytes) is NOT explicitly enforced in Erigon - it's enforced implicitly by constructing arrays of matching length from the sidecar structure (lines 52-71) before passing to ckzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. Column.Len() drives cellIndices length (line 52-55), and the sidecar structure enforces that Column contains cells matching KzgCommitments count.

P2P gossip validation calls verifyDataColumnSidecar at data_column_sidecar_service.go:114 which enforces KzgCommitments.Len() == KzgProofs.Len(). The equal-length constraint for all four arrays is NOT explicitly checked at P2P layer - it relies on SSZ deserialization schema and the implicit structure of DataColumnSidecar where Column contains one cell per commitment.

Go's memory safety prevents crash from array length mismatch within Erigon code. If arrays passed to ckzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch have mismatched lengths, the c-kzg-4844 library should return an error which is caught at line 74-77 and converted to false return. Crash potential depends on c-kzg-4844's handling of mismatched inputs.

VERIFIED: Array construction in VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs (lines 51-71) occurs BEFORE the ckzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch call (line 73). The arrays are constructed from sidecar fields, ensuring they have consistent lengths based on sidecar structure. cellIndices uses sidecar.Column.Len(), ckzgCommitments uses sidecar.KzgCommitments.Len(), ckzgCells uses sidecar.Column.Len(), ckzgProofs uses sidecar.KzgProofs.Len(). Prior validation at VerifyDataColumnSidecar ensures KzgCommitments.Len() == KzgProofs.Len().

Cell index validation is NOT explicitly enforced in Erigon before passing to coset functions. In VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs, cellIndices are set to sidecar.Index (the column index) for all entries (lines 52-55). The sidecar.Index is validated against NumberOfColumns in VerifyDataColumnSidecar (line 31), but this is different from CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The actual cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB validation must occur in c-kzg-4844 library.

P2P gossip validation checks sidecar.Index >= NumberOfColumns at cl/das/p2p_utils.go:31-33 and rejects invalid column indices. However, NumberOfColumns (typically 128) equals CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, so this validation effectively enforces cell_index bounds at the column level. Each cell in a DataColumnSidecar shares the same cell index (the column index), so the bounds check is satisfied.

P2P-delivered DataColumnSidecars are validated through verifyDataColumnSidecar (line 114) which checks Index < NumberOfColumns. Attacker cannot inject out-of-range cell_index via P2P because the sidecar.Index IS the cell_index used for all cells in the column, and it's bounds-checked before cryptographic operations.

VERIFIED: The cell_index bounds validation sequence is: 1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < NumberOfColumns (line 31-33), 2) VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs uses sidecar.Index as cellIndices[i] for all i (lines 52-55). Since VerifyDataColumnSidecar is called BEFORE VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs in ProcessMessage (data_column_sidecar_service.go:114 vs 168), bounds are validated before passing to coset functions in c-kzg library.

Integer overflow in FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index computation is NOT applicable to Erigon's Go code. Erigon passes cell_index (uint64) to c-kzg-4844 which handles the multiplication internally. Go's integer overflow behavior is defined (wrapping), but the actual multiplication and array access occurs in C code within c-kzg-4844. The bounds check (Index < NumberOfColumns) in Erigon ensures cell_index is within valid range before the library call.

Byte length validation is enforced by Go type system and SSZ schema. KZGCommitment is [48]byte (column_sidecar.go uses solid.NewStaticListSSZ with element size 48), KZGProof is [48]byte, Cell is [2048]byte (BytesPerCell constant at line 18). SSZ deserialization enforces these fixed sizes - malformed byte lengths cause DecodeSSZ to fail. No explicit runtime length check needed because Go's fixed-size arrays enforce this.

Incorrect commitment_bytes length cannot reach Erigon's KZG functions. SSZ deserialization of DataColumnSidecar enforces KZGCommitment as 48-byte fixed array (solid.NewStaticListSSZ with element size 48). Malformed P2P messages with wrong commitment length fail at SSZ decode before reaching VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs. Go's type system then ensures the 48-byte array is passed correctly to c-kzg.

Incorrect cell length cannot reach Erigon's KZG functions. Cell is defined as [BytesPerCell]byte where BytesPerCell=2048 (line 18, 102). SSZ deserialization enforces this fixed size. Malformed P2P messages with wrong cell length fail at SSZ decode. The solid.NewStaticListSSZ for Column uses BytesPerCell as element size (line 58).

Incorrect proof_bytes length cannot reach Erigon's KZG functions. KZGProof is 48 bytes enforced by solid.NewStaticListSSZ with element size 48 (line 64). SSZ deserialization rejects proofs with incorrect length before reaching cryptographic operations.

VERIFIED: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks KzgCommitments.Len() == KzgProofs.Len() at lines 41-43. Column (cells) length matches because DataColumnSidecar structure requires one cell per commitment (same blob structure). The array consistency is enforced by the SSZ schema where Column, KzgCommitments, and KzgProofs have matching element counts for valid sidecars.

P2P gossip validation enforces byte length constraints through SSZ schema at deserialization time. The DataColumnSidecar.DecodeSSZ (line 75-77) uses fixed-size element specifications: Column cells are BytesPerCell (2048), KzgCommitments are 48 bytes, KzgProofs are 48 bytes. Defense in depth: SSZ layer enforces sizes, then VerifyDataColumnSidecar validates count consistency.

BLS12-381 G1 subgroup check is implemented in c-kzg-4844 library, not Erigon. Erigon passes raw commitment bytes to ckzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch which internally deserializes and validates points. The bytes_to_kzg_commitment function with subgroup checks is in the external library. Erigon's responsibility is only to pass correctly sized byte arrays (48 bytes), which it does via type system.

BLS12-381 G1 subgroup check for proofs is implemented in c-kzg-4844 library, not Erigon. The bytes_to_kzg_proof function with subgroup validation is external. Erigon correctly passes 48-byte proof arrays via ckzg.Bytes48 type conversion at cl/das/p2p_utils.go:68-71.

Impact of non-subgroup points on pairing check is determined by c-kzg-4844's cryptographic implementation. Erigon does not implement pairing operations - it relies entirely on the external library. Analysis of subgroup attack impact requires auditing the c-kzg-4844 library itself.

Subgroup check bypass via crafted DataColumnSidecar would require bypassing c-kzg-4844's deserialization validation. Erigon passes raw bytes to the library which performs subgroup checks during point deserialization. The attack surface is in the external library, not Erigon.

VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs implicitly trusts that c-kzg-4844 will validate subgroup membership during VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. Erigon does NOT perform explicit subgroup validation - it passes byte arrays and trusts the library. This is appropriate delegation but creates dependency on external library correctness.

BLS12-381 subgroup check implementation is in c-kzg-4844 which uses the BLST library (Supranational). Erigon does not directly use or configure the cryptographic library - this is handled by c-kzg-4844's initialization. Correctness verification requires external library audit.

Commitment deduplication logic is implemented in c-kzg-4844's VerifyCellKZGProofBatch, not in Erigon. Erigon passes non-deduplicated arrays (one commitment per cell) at cl/das/p2p_utils.go:57-60 where each commitment from KzgCommitments is included for each cell. The library performs any necessary deduplication internally.

Commitment_indices mapping bijectivity is an internal property of c-kzg-4844's batch verification algorithm. Erigon does not implement this mapping - it passes arrays to the library and receives a boolean result.

Exploitation of commitment deduplication to forge proofs would target c-kzg-4844's algorithm, not Erigon. Erigon's role is to correctly construct input arrays from DataColumnSidecar (which it does at p2p_utils.go:57-71) and reject verification failures.

Impact of commitment deduplication failure on validator-node is mediated through Erigon's handling of verification results. If c-kzg-4844 returns error (caught at p2p_utils.go:74) or false, Erigon rejects the sidecar. Consensus impact requires actual proof forgery in the library.

The 50% cell threshold for recovery is enforced by c-kzg-4844's RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs function, not Erigon. Erigon's wrapper at das_utils.go:154-176 passes cellIndices and cells directly to ckzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (line 161) without explicit threshold validation. The library returns error if threshold is not met.

50% threshold derivation from CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB is computed in c-kzg-4844 library. CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB constant is defined in Erigon at cl/das/utils/block_produce_utils.go:13 as 128, but the actual threshold enforcement occurs in the external library during recovery.

Cell withholding attack triggering incorrect polynomial recovery depends on c-kzg-4844's threshold enforcement. Erigon's wrapper passes whatever cells are available and handles errors at line 162-164. If library incorrectly allows recovery with <50% cells, Erigon would use the incorrect result.

Blast radius of insufficient-cell recovery is determined by how Erigon uses recovered data. At das_utils.go:132-148, RecoverMatrix uses recovered cells to build matrix entries. If recovery produces incorrect polynomial (due to library bug), incorrect cells/proofs propagate. Post-recovery verification would be needed to catch this.

Cell count pre-condition is NOT explicitly checked in Erigon before calling c-kzg recovery. RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (lines 154-176) performs array conversion (155-158) then immediately calls ckzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (161). No explicit len(cells) >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 check exists in Erigon - this relies entirely on library validation.

Cell_indices uniqueness and ascending order are NOT validated in Erigon before recovery. RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs passes cellIndices directly to ckzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs without sorting or uniqueness checks. The library must enforce these constraints. In RecoverMatrix (line 122-129), cells are collected from partialMatrix without deduplication.

Polynomial interpolation assumptions about unique, sorted cell_indices are internal to c-kzg-4844. Erigon does not implement interpolation - it relies on ckzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs. Duplicate handling behavior is determined by the library.

POTENTIAL ISSUE: RecoverMatrix collects cells from partialMatrix without deduplication (lines 122-129). If partialMatrix contains duplicate entries for the same RowIndex+ColumnIndex (from different P2P sources), both would be passed to RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs. This could cause issues if cells conflict or if library doesn't handle duplicates.

Cell_indices range validation [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) is NOT explicitly performed in Erigon before recovery. RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs accepts cellIndices as []ColumnIndex (uint64) without bounds checking. The library must validate ranges. For DataColumnSidecar processing, the Index is validated against NumberOfColumns in VerifyDataColumnSidecar.

Crash or undefined behavior in coset_for_cell with out-of-range cell_index is determined by c-kzg-4844's implementation. Erigon does not implement coset functions - they are internal to the library. The library's C code behavior with invalid indices requires separate audit.

For P2P-delivered DataColumnSidecars, out-of-range cell_indices are prevented by VerifyDataColumnSidecar's Index < NumberOfColumns check. However, for recovery operations (RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs), cell_indices come from partialMatrix which may not have been validated through the same path. Attacker cannot directly inject via gossip but may influence through other means.

Cell_index range validation does NOT occur before resource allocation in Erigon's recovery wrapper. RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs allocates ckzgCells array (line 155) before any validation. Library call follows at line 161. Validation occurs within the library, after Erigon's allocation.

CRITICAL GAP: Post-recovery KZG commitment verification is NOT performed in Erigon's RecoverMatrix. After RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (line 132), recovered cells/proofs are directly added to matrix (lines 138-147) WITHOUT verification against original commitments. The note in property 'recovery function DOES NOT verify commitment consistency - caller MUST do it' appears unimplemented.

CRITICAL: RecoverMatrix (the primary caller of RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs) does NOT verify recovered data against original commitment. After recovery at line 132, cells are used directly without calling any verification function. This matches the property's warning that 'caller MUST do it' - but the caller (RecoverMatrix) does not.

POTENTIAL VULNERABILITY: A malicious P2P peer providing corrupted cells could cause RecoverMatrix to produce incorrect recovered cells that are NOT verified before being returned. The matrix entries (lines 138-147) containing potentially incorrect cells/proofs could propagate. Verification should occur before returning from RecoverMatrix.

Erigon DOES trust reconstructed data without cryptographic verification in RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs. The function converts recovered cells (lines 166-169) and proofs (lines 171-174) and returns them directly. No verification against any commitment occurs. Caller is expected to verify but RecoverMatrix does not.

Original_commitment source verification is NOT APPLICABLE to current Erigon implementation because RecoverMatrix does not perform any commitment verification at all. The function does not have access to commitments - it only operates on cells and indices from partialMatrix. To fix CHK-0141/0142/0143, commitments would need to be passed to RecoverMatrix.

Polynomial degree validation before truncation in recover_polynomialcoeff is internal to c-kzg-4844. Erigon does not implement polynomial recovery - it calls ckzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs which handles this internally. Degree validation logic is in the external library.

Validator node does NOT detect incorrect polynomials from recovery because Erigon's RecoverMatrix does not perform post-recovery commitment verification (as noted in CHK-0141/0142). If the library produces an incorrect polynomial due to truncation issues, Erigon would not catch it.

Whether P2P peer can craft cell data to force polynomial degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB depends on c-kzg-4844's mathematical implementation. Erigon passes raw cells to the library. This is a cryptographic property that must be verified in the external library.

Division by zero prevention in recover_polynomialcoeff (ez_over_coset / zp_over_coset) is handled by c-kzg-4844's implementation. The coset shift by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY ensuring Z(x) has no roots is a cryptographic invariant maintained by the library, not Erigon.

PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY definition and verification is part of c-kzg-4844's trusted setup and constants, not Erigon code. Erigon uses the library without configuring cryptographic parameters. Correctness of this constant requires auditing the external library and its trusted setup.
